story.title: Nothing teases screen-less product launching next month, ‘couldn’t have been an app’ - 9to5Google

facts.text: He didn’t give away much about what exactly the new device is, only that one feature it won’t have is a screen: > “Our first AI-native product ships next month.
Nothing CEO Carl Pei said in a post on X that the company’s launching its first AI device in December.
It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.” Pei shared an image with the post that says “NOTHING(R)” in the top left corner, above an ambiguous black rounded corner.
It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.
Pei has teased an AI-first device for some time and the company has also said that it plans to release a pair of AI-linked smart glasses, as well as earbuds with AI integrations.

On Wednesday, CEO Carl Pei posted on X that the company’s first “AI-native product” ships in December. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.
It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app,” Pei wrote.

Our first AI-native product ships next month.
It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.
It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.
The screen-less design certainly limits a lot of other possibilities.
In a post on Twitter/X , Nothing CEO Carl Pei says that the company is launching a new product in December.

The rest of Pei’s post talks about how the AI industry is searching for its ideal product and the tools we’ve used over the years, and really seems to imply Nothing’s product will be an ambient recorder of some kind when discussing the “context gap.” The most telling bit reads:
Nothing has confirmed that it will launch a new “AI-native” product in December, which the brand says “couldn't have been an application”.
Reports suggest that the product could be a recorder, which would align with what Nothing has been working on.
Nothing plans to bring in a product comes after the likes of Amazon and a few other brands have started to dabble in AI-based voice recorders.
